intro_md: 📖 **6 min.** You read this story on Thursday. Read it again **faster** – a known story is the best way to train reading speed without translating.

parts.title: Fast re-read: Episode 2
parts.md:
⏱ **Note the time when you start.** Read at a comfortable speed, **never go back**. Last time you needed 4 minutes – can you do it in 3?

> The café on the corner of Hope Street was small and warm. It smelled of coffee and fresh bread, and there were only six tables. A young woman with short red hair was standing behind the counter.
>
> "Morning! What can I get you?" she asked.
>
> "A coffee, please," Nam said. "And… something to eat. I'm not sure what's good."
>
> She smiled. "Then try the bacon sandwich. Everyone says it's the best in Manchester. I'm Jess, <mark>by the way</mark>. I haven't seen you before."
>
> "I'm Nam. I <mark>moved in</mark> yesterday – number fourteen."
>
> "Margaret's building? <mark>Lucky you</mark>. She knows everything about everyone on this street." Jess laughed. "Did the heating wake you up?"
>
> Nam stared at her. "How do you know about the heating?"
>
> "Everyone knows about the heating."
>
> Nam sat by the window with his coffee. Outside, people were walking quickly to work under black umbrellas. He felt tired, **but** he also felt something else – something he hadn't felt yesterday. He <mark>felt a little bit at home</mark>.
>
> The sandwich arrived. Jess was right: it was very good.
>
> **While** he was eating, he checked his phone. There was a message from his new manager, Claire: *"Welcome to the team! See you at 9. Don't worry about being on time today – the trains are terrible."*
>
> Nam looked at the clock. It was 8:15. **Although** Claire said not to worry, he didn't want to be late on his first day. He finished his coffee, said goodbye to Jess and stepped out into the rain.
>
> Twenty minutes later, he was standing outside a tall glass building. His shoes were wet, his hair was wet, and his heart was beating fast. He <mark>took a deep breath</mark> and pushed the door.
>
> "You must be Nam," said a woman with grey glasses. "I'm Claire. Come in – you look like you need another coffee."
>
> Nam laughed. It was only his second day in Manchester, and he was already <mark>getting used to</mark> two things: the rain, and people offering him coffee.
